i18n:
8. Internationalization (i18n)

8.1 Creating a Language File

Create a separate JSON file for each language. The top-level key is the module ID:

// i18n/en/modules/my_module.json
{
    "my_module": {
        "title":        "My Module",
        "description":  "Description of the module",
        "btn_save":     "Save",
        "btn_cancel":   "Cancel",
        "errors": {
            "not_found": "Not found",
            "save_failed": "Error saving"
        }
    }
}

8.2 Using in HTML — data-i18n

Mark texts in the template with data-i18n. The key is the path in the JSON file (dot notation):

<h1 data-i18n="my_module.title">My Module</h1>
<p  data-i18n="my_module.description"></p>
<button data-i18n="my_module.btn_save">Save</button>

<!-- For Placeholder -->
<input data-i18n-placeholder="my_module.search" placeholder="Search...">

8.3 Loading Language — loadLanguage()

Load the language in the extra_js block of the template. This automatically loads all core files + the module language file:

{% block extra_js %}
<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
    if (typeof loadLanguage === 'function') {
        loadLanguage('{{ current_lang|default:"en" }}', 'my_module');
    }
});
</script>
{% endblock %}

loadLanguage(lang, moduleId) loads in this order:

  1. i18n/{lang}/core-common.json — global labels
  2. i18n/{lang}/ui-components.json — UI texts
  3. i18n/{lang}/help-modal.json — help texts
  4. i18n/{lang}/modules/my_module.json — module texts

8.4 Subdirectory Structure (for large modules)

For modules with many texts (like documentation), the language file can be split into subdirectories. The system automatically detects if a manifest.json exists:

i18n/en/modules/my_module/
├── manifest.json          ← List of all files
├── meta.json              ← Module metadata
├── 01_overview.json       ← Chapter 1
├── 02_details.json        ← Chapter 2
└── 03_settings.json       ← Chapter 3
// manifest.json
{
    "files": [
        "meta.json",
        "01_overview.json",
        "02_details.json",
        "03_settings.json"
    ]
}

8.5 New Translation with the i18n Translator

After creating the German language file, automatically translate into all other languages:

# Check if all languages are complete
python3 apps/abpe_ui/bin/i18n_translator.py --check

# Add missing translations
python3 apps/abpe_ui/bin/i18n_translator.py

# Only one language
python3 apps/abpe_ui/bin/i18n_translator.py --lang fr

8.6 Translations in JavaScript — t()

// Simple text
const title = t('my_module.title');

// With fallback
const label = t('my_module.btn_save') || 'Save';

// In dynamic HTML
container.innerHTML = `
    <h3>${t('my_module.section_title')}</h3>
    <p>${t('my_module.description')}</p>
    <button onclick="save()">${t('my_module.btn_save')}</button>
`;

8.7 Adding a New Language

Via the admin area → System → Language packages: Select language from dropdown and install. Or via CLI:

# Install new language (automatically translates all files)
python3 apps/abpe_ui/bin/add_new_language.py --add es

# Hide language
python3 apps/abpe_ui/bin/add_new_language.py --hide it

# Show language again
python3 apps/abpe_ui/bin/add_new_language.py --show it
